name: Shemida
overview: Shemida is a male figure from the tribe of Manasseh, identified uniquely as the son of Gilead. He is noted in Scripture for being the progenitor of the Shemidaites, a clan named after him. His mention is concise but establishes his place within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemida is a proper name that possibly means 'the name knows' or 'Eshmun has known,' reflecting Hebrew linguistic roots. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but its meaning may carry significance relating to knowledge or recognition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shemida as the son of Gilead. Additional inferred paternal relationships connect him to Ahian, Shechem, Lihki, and Aniam, suggesting a lineage within the Manasseh tribe, though these are not directly stated but inferred from 1 Chronicles 7:19. Beyond these, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shemida's significance lies in his role as the ancestor of the Shemidaites, marking him as an important tribal figure within Manasseh. His genealogy helps trace the development of Israelite clans and tribal identities, underscoring the biblical emphasis on lineage and inheritance. Though briefly mentioned, his inclusion in the census and genealogical records highlights the faithfulness of Scripture in preserving the heritage of God's people.
